ESR1 mutations and MAPK pathway alterations show a trend toward mutual exclusivity in post-hormonal therapy HR+HER2- tumors, reaching borderline significance.

Primary analysis (mutation-only, per-patient, n=656): Fisher's exact test odds ratio = 0.39, p = 0.050. Of 656 patients, 121 (18.4%) carry ESR1 mutations and 58 (8.8%) carry MAPK pathway mutations. Only 5 patients (0.8%) carry both — approximately half the 10.7 expected under independence, consistent with mutual exclusivity.

Comprehensive analysis (mutations + CNA amplifications/deletions, n=656): Fisher's exact test OR = 0.62, p = 0.213. With broader MAPK alteration definition (78 patients), 10 have both ESR1 and MAPK alterations vs 14.4 expected. The trend remains toward mutual exclusivity but is not statistically significant.

Subgroup finding — NF1 loss specifically is significantly mutually exclusive with ESR1 mutations (OR = 0.23, Fisher's exact p = 0.031). NF1 loss-of-function (mutations + deep deletions) is found in 39 patients (5.9%), of whom only 2 also carry ESR1 mutations.

Non-NF1 core MAPK cascade mutations (KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, RAF, MEK, ERK) are rare in this cohort (28/656 = 4.3%) and show a non-significant trend toward mutual exclusivity with ESR1 (OR = 0.52, p = 0.45).

Interpretation: ESR1 mutations and MAPK pathway alterations — primarily driven by NF1 loss — represent alternative, non-overlapping routes to endocrine therapy resistance in HR+HER2- breast cancer. The finding is consistent with prior reports that NF1 loss is enriched in endocrine-resistant advanced breast cancer and that ESR1 mutations and NF1 alterations occur in distinct patient subsets. The borderline statistical significance warrants replication in larger cohorts.
